title: USB Blend D formulation
brief: USB Blend D as written by Dutch (Ramaj), 2026-09-05 (source sha256 d143a16fd4d87980…)
disclaimers: No claim in the source text is established by the text itself: each one needs the test listed for it.
The density is a conditional rule-of-mixtures estimate (assumptions A1–A4), not a measurement.
caveats: Stated ranges don't fix the total: Ingredient ranges sum to 86 % (all at minimum) to 103 % (all at maximum). 'Total: 100 %' is reachable but not determined by the ranges, so an explicit version with exact fractions is required (one is proposed by a recorded rule).

Composition basis not stated: Percentages carry no basis (wt%, vol%?). Compounding recipes are normally by mass, but the source must say; the density estimate assumes mass basis and shows the volume-basis reading alongside.

'Cure temperature' for a thermoplastic: HDPE is a thermoplastic: it is melt-processed (melted, shaped, cooled), not cured. 200 °C is above HDPE's ~133 °C melting peak and within typical 180–220 °C HDPE melt temperatures, so it is recorded as a melt-processing temperature in the process version. Missing: where it is measured (barrel/melt/mould), time at temperature, equipment, cooling profile.

'Hydrogen stays contained' conflicts with the literature: Hydrogen permeates HDPE (permeation is 'inevitable' in HDPE/PA Type IV liners; HDPE H2 permeability 5.88×10⁻¹⁴ cm³·cm/(cm²·s·Pa) at 288 K, 70 MPa, ~3.4× PA6). Containment is UNSUPPORTED for Blend D pending permeation testing of the compound (ASTM D1434 / ISO 15105-1 screening; CSA/ANSI CHMC 2 or ISO 11114-5 at pressure) and vessel-level qualification (ISO 19881 / SAE J2579), including after impact.

'Inherently resistant to hydrogen' / 'no degradation' overstated: No metal-type embrittlement, but dissolved hydrogen plasticises HDPE and decompression can blister or collapse liners. Needs exposure + decompression-cycle testing (CSA/ANSI CHMC 2) at the service pressure and temperature.

HDPE base: grade, supplier, meltFlowRate not specified: HDPE grade and melt flow rate (MFI) are unspecified; density (0.941–0.970 g/cm³ across grades), stiffness, impact and processability depend on the grade.

HDPE/HC co-polymer: grade, supplier, variant, meltFlowRate not specified: 'HDPE/HC co-polymer' is not identifiable: comonomer(s), grade and supplier unknown. Its density is UNKNOWN and it blocks the strict density estimate.

Basalt fiber: grade, supplier, fiberLength, fiberDiameter, sizing not specified: Basalt fibre length (chopped vs milled vs continuous), diameter and sizing (silane/PE-compatible?) are unspecified; reinforcement in HDPE depends on them.
CaCO3: grade, supplier, particleSize, surfaceTreatment, purity not specified: CaCO3 grade is unspecified (ground vs precipitated, particle size, stearate surface treatment).

Graphene: grade, supplier, variant, particleSize, surfaceTreatment not specified: Graphene grade is unspecified: graphene nanoplatelets (multi-layer stacks, µm lateral size) and few-layer/monolayer graphene differ widely in thickness, surface area and dispersion, so claims attributed to 'graphene' are underspecified; the density used assumes nanoplatelets.

Silica: grade, supplier, particleSize, surfaceTreatment, purity not specified: Silica form is unspecified (fumed, precipitated or crystalline): density (2.2 amorphous vs 2.65 quartz g/cm³) and handling hazards differ by form; get the supplier SDS for the actual grade.

Process underspecified: Not stated: equipment (extruder type, screw configuration); mixing order / feeding points; residence time and screw speed; filler drying; forming method (injection, compression, rotational moulding, extrusion); cooling profile; post-processing / conditioning.
Wording that names no measurable property or condition: 'structural integrity' and 'splitting cycles' need a measurable definition (which property, which conditions).
Comparisons with the 'marine blend' can't be checked: The marine blend's formulation and data aren't on record; ingest it as its own source record first.

Ingredient roles are hypotheses about the composite: Each ingredient's stated role (e.g. 'graphene: thermal conductivity') is a claim about the COMPOSITE. Constituent properties do not predict composite behaviour (dispersion, interface, loading thresholds), so none of these is computed from constituents; each needs a composite test.

Claims only a finished part can settle: Containment, seal integrity and pressure resistance belong to the vessel (geometry, wall, liner, fittings), not the material; material tests are necessary but not sufficient (ISO 19881 / SAE J2579).

Density only estimable under an assumption: The strict rule-of-mixtures density is UNKNOWN because the HDPE/HC copolymer has no cited density. A conditional estimate (assumption A1: polyethylene-family 0.910–0.970 g/cm³) is reported separately, for screening only.

No SDS on record for any constituent; intended use is a hydrogen pressure vessel: Hazards depend on the exact grades (e.g. silica form, nanoplatelet handling): attach each supplier's SDS. A hydrogen pressure-containing part is a regulated application; acceptance must come from the vessel standard (ISO 19881 / SAE J2579), not from material claims.

physicalTests: As-made composition (filler and fibre loading) (P0 prerequisite): thermogravimetric compositional analysis (polymer vs inorganic residue) of each batch [[object Object]]; ash content: total inorganic loading (basalt + CaCO3 + silica) against the formulation version [[object Object]]
Density (P0 prerequisite): density / specific gravity by displacement, on compression- or injection-moulded specimens of the exact formulation and process version [[object Object]]
Melt flow rate (P0 prerequisite): melt flow rate of the HDPE grade and of the compound (190 °C / 2.16 kg is the usual PE condition) [[object Object]]

Processing (melt) temperature (P0 prerequisite): DSC of the HDPE grade and of the compound to fix the melt window; melt flow rate at the stated temperature range to check processability [[object Object], [object Object]]
Melting and crystallisation temperatures (P0 prerequisite): DSC melting / crystallisation peaks: fixes the melt-processing window the 'cure temperature' must sit in [[object Object]]

Compatibility with hydrogen (property change after exposure, rapid decompression, blistering) (P1 safety-critical): polymer compatibility in compressed hydrogen: property retention after exposure and decompression cycles [[object Object]]; compatibility assessment of non-metallic materials with the gas content (guidance) [[object Object]]

Hydrogen permeability / permeation rate (P1 safety-critical): differential-pressure H2 transmission rate and permeability on sheet specimens (screening, low pressure) [[object Object], [object Object]]; high-pressure hydrogen permeation (HPHP method) at service pressure and temperature, specimens made by the production process [[object Object], [object Object]]

Pressure resistance (P1 safety-critical): long-term creep and creep-rupture of the material under the stress the wall will see [[object Object]]; hydraulic burst and pressure-cycle qualification of the finished container [[object Object]]

Containment / seal integrity of the finished vessel (incl. after impact) (P1 safety-critical): vessel-level qualification (permeation, pressure cycling, drop/impact, burst) on the finished container; a material coupon cannot establish this [[object Object], [object Object]]

Impact resistance (notched pendulum and instrumented puncture) (P2 performance): notched Izod impact energy (ASTM and ISO results are not interchangeable: pick one system and keep it) [[object Object], [object Object]]; notched Charpy impact energy [[object Object], [object Object]]; instrumented high-speed puncture: load-displacement curve, energy to peak and to failure, ductile vs brittle failure mode; repeat at the lowest service temperature [[object Object]]

Resistance to salt water (P2 performance): immersion in ASTM D1141 substitute ocean water per ASTM D543; report mass, dimension and appearance change and ASTM D638 property retention [[object Object], [object Object], [object Object]]
Surface hardness (P2 performance): Shore D durometer hardness against the unfilled base resin as control [[object Object]]

Tensile strength, modulus and elongation at break (P2 performance): tensile strength, modulus and elongation at break (elongation is the 'no added brittleness' check); fibre-reinforced compounds need flow-direction and cross-flow specimens [[object Object]]

Thermal conductivity (P2 performance): thermal conductivity by transient plane source (hot disc), in-plane and through-thickness [[object Object]]; thermal diffusivity by flash (conductivity also needs density and specific heat) [[object Object]]
Weathering and UV stability (P2 performance): fluorescent-UV cycle exposure per ASTM G154, then tensile and impact retention vs unexposed controls [[object Object], [object Object], [object Object]]

Viscoelastic response and shape recovery after deformation (P2 performance): creep under constant load, then unload and record recovery over time (the 'returns to shape' claim) [[object Object]]; sub-perforation impacts at increasing energy, then measure residual dent depth after a stated recovery time (no single standard defines 'springs back'; the acceptance threshold must be set for the part) [[object Object]]
